ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  Monday, November 08, 2021, at 6:30 p.m.
  La Verne City Hall - Council Chambers,
  3660 D Street, La Verne, CA 91750

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk’s
Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting. Regular Meetings are held on the 1st and
3rd Monday of every month.

The Council Chambers will be opened to the public. In an effort to keep a safe environment and to minimize
the spread of the COVID-19 Virus, masking will be required for all in attendance. To facilitate public
participation for those who do not wish to attend in person, the meeting will still be made available virtually to
residents. Below are the following opportunities on how to participate:

1)  View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org and click on the green
  “Council Meeting Live Stream” button.

2)  Individuals can email their comments to the Assistant City Clerk at cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org up to
  noon on the day of the meeting. Those comments will be shared with City Council in advance of the
  City Council meeting and included as part of the permanent record. Please be advised that
  public comments submitted by emails or any other format to the City are public records
  that will be made available for public viewing.

3)  Individuals who wish to share their comments directly during the meeting may do so by emailing
  the Assistant City Clerk at cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org with their phone number and the item(s)
  they wish to speak on. Requests will be accepted before and throughout the meeting and staff will
  call you back at the appropriate time. Once items are considered by the City Council, no further
  public comment on that matter will be accepted. A time limit of 3-minutes is set for all public
  comments.

4)  If you wish to participate via Zoom, you will need to register at
  https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_RRsYxY8BRU-z5I54NIksNA
  before 5:00 p.m. on Monday, November 8, 2021, and please be aware that space is limited. You will have
  the ability to watch the meeting in real time and raise your hand to request to comment as appropriate on
  the current agenda item(s). Once it is your turn to speak, you will be brought into the meeting and have the
  ability to turn your video on when called upon.
 Agenda, Adjourned City Council Meeting, Monday, November 08, 2021, Page 2

1.  CALL TO ORDER

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

3.  ROLL CALL:  Council Member Lau, Council Member Crosby, Council Member Carder,
  Mayor Pro Tem Davis and Mayor Hepburn.

4.  Assessment of Fire Operations - The Fire Chief will provide the City Council with an
  overview of his assessment on various aspects of Fire Department operations and
  recommendations for initial improvements.

5.  Adjournment.

  THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING of the La Verne City Council
  is on Monday, November 15, 2021, at 6:30p.m.

 How Did We Get Here?
• La Verne Fire Department History & Evolvement

• Station 3 Implementation & Staffing

• FD Ripe for New Direction
   What do we know?
• Desire to maintain LVFD
• LVFD not meeting industry (NFPA, ISO) standards for:
  • Distance between stations
  • Geographic & response time inequity
  • Effective response force (At least 50% of initial full alarm assignment)
• LVFD failing to meet standing auto aid obligations - recent increase in LACoFD requests
• Private ambulance provider not interested in maintaining current agreement
• Unanticipated $217,000 loss to private provider since implementation (General Fund Impact)
• $1.7 million specialty apparatus not being used, funded in part by private investment
• LVFD failing to meet State Fire Training Requirements (capacity to train)
• LVFD failing to meet State Fire Marshal mandated inspections (capacity to inspect)
• No succession planning
• CA Fire Service contending with state wide private ambulance crisis
• LVFD far below regional per station funding average (comparable municipal agencies)
• La Verne has demonstrated desire to invest in its FD already

  Auto & Mutual Aid Imbalance
38% increase in demand for LACoFD resources
  (91 reciprocal requests from LACoFD for LVFD Resources)
 Redeployment Recommendation
Sequentially Dependent

1. Create 12 EMT “Ambulance Operator” (A/O) positions

2. Utilize A/Os to staff rescue ambulance 761 & 762

3. Reclassify two FF positions & move suppression personnel to heavy apparatus

4. Reopen fire station 3 with a Paramedic fire engine

5. Place quint ladder truck in service at station 1

6. Renegotiate Auto & Mutual Agreements

7. Implement department wide succession planning
 Redeployment Benefits
• Institutes first significant change to LVFD in 15 years
• Introduces lower cost workforce into the Fire Department
• Sustainable model using current revenue projections
• Paramedics more available for City responses
• Reduced response times to all areas of the City
• Increased availability of personnel for critical calls
• Quick response to biggest target hazard
• Career growth opportunity for personnel
• Capacity to meet State training and inspection requirements
• Wildland Urban Interface proactive engagement
• La Verne reduces exposure to Statewide private ambulance crisis
• La Verne FD ambulances assistance to surrounding cities

• Commitment to staff second ambulance while A/O program is implemented (1/2022)
• Focus efforts on numerous lost administrative revenues
